candidates.context: This guidance describes FDA’s recommendations to investigational new drug sponsors for 21 setting endotoxin limits during the development of investigational drugs intended for use in 22 combination with other approved drugs or for the codevelopment of two or more investigational 23 drugs. The scope of this guidance is limited to anticancer drugs, including combination products 24 under 21 CFR Part 3, 4 as described further in this guidance and administered parenterally (except 25 for intraocular administration) to treat serious and life-threatening cancers based on histology or 26 stage of disease. candidates.statement: In keeping with the principles of facilitating drug development for serious and life-threatening 136 diseases, this guidance outlines FDA’s current thinking on a risk-based approach to setting 137 acceptance criteria for endotoxins during the clinical development of drugs intended to treat 138 serious and life-threatening cancers. Additionally, sponsors should refer to recommendations 139 regarding testing discussed in the guidance for industry Pyrogen and Endotoxins Testing: 140 Questions and Answers . 141
candidates.context: IV. SETTING ENDOTOXIN LIMITS DURING DRUG DEVELOPMENT 134 A. Early Clinical Development 143

candidates.statement: • For investigational products that are small molecules or certain therapeutic biological 151 products, 7 the endotoxin limits of an investigational drug or the combined endotoxin 152 limits of multiple investigational drugs administered concomitantly by a parenteral route 153 should not exceed the limit specified in USP General Chapter <85>, that is, 5 USP-EU 154 per kg body weight per hour or 100 EU per m 2 body surface area (BSA) per hour. The 155 sponsor of an investigational new drug need not consider the potential endotoxin 156 contribution from approved and/or licensed components of a combination regimen when 157 calculating the acceptable limits for endotoxin exposure from the investigational drug. 158

candidates.statement: When investigational products will be administered intrathecally with other agents, the combined 170 endotoxin exposure from all drugs (investigational drug and other concomitantly administered 171 investigational, approved, or licensed drugs) should not exceed that specified in USP General 172 Chapter <85>, that is, 0.2 USP-EU per kg body weight per hour. 173

candidates.statement: • Sponsors should tighten the specifications for endotoxin limits to ensure that by the time 188 they submit a marketing application for that drug, the endotoxin limits will not exceed 189 that specified in USP General Chapter < 85 > for a parenterally administered drug 190 considering the combined endotoxin exposure of the investigational drug and all 191 concomitantly administered drugs cited in the INDICATIONS AND USAGE section of 192 product labeling. 193
